Securities\nCompany Report\n1Q26 earnings call key Q&As\n1. Is Samsung pursuing multi-year memory supply agreements, and how will\nincentive bonus provisions be reflected?\n- Details on multi-year memory contracts are restricted under NDAs. However, major customers are\nrequesting volume commitments based on confidence in AI-driven mid- to long-term demand.\nSamsung is pursuing multi-year contracts within its available supply, with some agreements already\nsigned.\n- These contracts carry stronger commitments than conventional agreements and help secure both\nbusiness stability and visibility amid rising risks around investment scale, duration, and technology\ncomplexity. Samsung plans to flexibly manage investments based on customer demand.\n- Incentive bonus provisions were not reflected in 1Q26 results, as labor-management discussions\nare still ongoing and payment terms/amounts have not been finalized. Recognition in 2Q26 will\ndepend on negotiation outcomes.\n2. What drove 1Q memory performance?\n- In 1Q26, AI demand increased on the spread of agentic AI, led by HBM, server DRAM, and server\nSSDs. With limited supply expansion capacity, the demand-supply gap widened.\n- Under a server-focused sales strategy, DRAM bit growth rose by low-teens QoQ and NAND by low-\n20s QoQ, marking record quarterly sales for servers. DRAM met guidance and NAND exceeded bit\nshipment guidance. ASPs rose by low-90s for DRAM and high-80s for NAND, supported by market\nprice increases and a server-driven mix improvement. The memory business once again delivered\nrecord quarterly results on strong demand and product competitiveness.\n9\nSamsung Electronics (005930 KS)\n3. What is the impact of the labor union strike on production and earnings?\n- The union has announced a general strike from May 21 to June 7. While the exact impact is difficult\nto assess, Samsung plans to minimize production disruption through a dedicated task force and\nresponse system. The company will prioritize an amicable resolution through labor-management\ndialogue.\n4. Will Samsung maintain its shareholder return policy, and what is its value\nenhancement strategy?\n- Samsung plans to execute its previously announced shareholder return policy as scheduled,\nkeeping shareholder value enhancement as a core management priority. The next policy is under\nreview by management and the board, and will be shared with the market once finalized.\n- For corporate value enhancement, Samsung is investing more than W10tn in facilities and R&D to\nstrengthen production hubs in Pyeongtaek, Taylor, and the Yongin cluster, while advancing next-\ngeneration technologies.\n- Samsung is also pursuing portfolio restructuring and mid- to long-term growth through M&A deals\nand venture investments, with continued investments in HVAC, automotive electronics, medical, and\nrobotics.\n10\nCompany Report\n5. What is the impact of Middle East geopolitical risk on supply chains/costs, and\nhow will MX defend profitability?\n- Semiconductor lines are operating normally, with no supply chain disruption since the Middle East\nconflict. Although Samsung imports some gases from the region, risks are limited given sufficient\nsafety inventory and logistics response systems.\n- The supply chain is diversified across regions including the US and Japan, allowing additional risk\nresponse. Power supply is expected to remain stable through government cooperation. Higher oil\nprices are increasing logistics costs, which Samsung is addressing through inventory optimization,\nstronger logistics partnerships, alternative transport options, and long-term freight contracts.\n- In MX, higher memory prices increased cost burden and hurt 1Q26 profitability YoY. The burden is\nlikely to continue in 2Q26, but Samsung plans to minimize profit declines through new product sales,\ncost efficiencies, and supply stabilization.\n6. What is the memory market outlook and 2Q26 bit growth guidance?\n- Memory market growth remains driven by AI demand. The spread of agentic AI is accelerating data\nprocessing needs and adoption of technologies that improve compute efficiency.\n- Supply expansion remains constrained by new fab lead times, while the supply shortage has\ndeepened to historically tight levels. Customers are already securing 2027 demand, which should\nfurther widen the supply-demand gap.\n- In 2Q26, Samsung will maintain a server-centric mix, with DRAM bit growth expected at mid-single\ndigits QoQ and NAND at low-single digits QoQ.\n11\nSamsung Electronics (005930 KS)\n7. What is Samsung’s humanoid robotics and physical AI strategy?\n- Robotics is becoming increasingly viable with advances in physical AI. Samsung is working to\ninternalize key components and develop customized parts. It will first focus on manufacturing-site\nrobots, then expand into home and retail applications. The strategy combines in-house development\nwith partnerships, investments, and acquisitions.\n8. What is the outlook for HBM, HBM4, and HBM4E?\n- HBM revenue is expected to more than triple YoY. HBM4 capacity has been fully sold out following\nthe industry’s first mass production, driven by strong customer demand. Ramp-up is underway, with\nsupply to expand meaningfully in 2H26. From 3Q26, HBM4 is expected to account for more than half\nof total HBM revenue, and also exceed 50% on a full-year basis. Samsung is developing HBM4E\nbased on 1c-nano technology, targeting 16Gbps and 4TB/s performance, with sample shipments\nplanned in 2Q26.\n9. How will Samsung respond to display price pressure and defend profitability?\n- Higher memory prices are increasing set makers’ cost burden, which could weigh on display demand\nand add price-cut pressure. Samsung is improving cost competitiveness through productivity gains\nand strengthening its premium portfolio. It plans to secure stable profitability by expanding\ndifferentiated technologies such as privacy protection technology, FnP, to enhance high-end\ncompetitiveness.\n10. What is the 2nm/4nm order status and foundry strategy?\n- Samsung is pursuing orders in high-growth areas including AI, HPC, automotive, and robotics. It is\nin 2nm collaboration discussions with multiple global customers, with some near-term results\nexpected. For 4nm, rising HBM base die demand is validating competitiveness and driving demand\ngrowth. Samsung is reviewing supply expansion plans.\n- It is also developing next-generation technologies such as silicon photonics and co-packaged optics\nwith global customers. The optical communications module project is scheduled for mass production\nin 2H26.\n12\nCompany Report\n11. What is the TV profitability strategy?\n- Amid raw material price hikes and market uncertainty, Samsung will target both premium and volume\nmarkets through Micro RGB, OLED, and Mini LED products. It plans to defend profitability by\nstrengthening World Cup-related marketing and expanding the services business.\n12. What is Samsung’s mix strategy between HBM and conventional DRAM?\n- Conventional DRAM profitability has improved near term on price increases, while HBM operates\nunder annual contracts and conventional DRAM under quarterly contracts, creating a temporary\nprofitability reversal. Demand for HBM and conventional DRAM is complementary in AI infrastructure\nbuildout. Samsung plans to maintain a balanced mix strategy focused on mid- to long-term growth\nand customer relationships rather than short-term profitability alone.\n13. What is the status of Exynos 2700 and the strategy for expanding non-memory\napplications?\n- Exynos 2700 development is progressing as planned, based on technology competitiveness from\nExynos 2600. Market share gains are expected in the next model through enhanced AI performance.\n- As AI demand shifts rapidly from training to inference, demand for customer-specific solutions is\nrising. Samsung will strengthen its ability to offer optimized architectures and solutions from data\ncenters to on-device applications, expanding beyond memory into system semiconductors.\n14. What is the MX product strategy and growth/profitability outlook?\n- MX is pursuing broad-based growth across all price tiers, from flagship to mid- and low-end. For\nS26, Samsung aims to boost consumer-perceived value and sales through performance upgrades\nand stronger core user experiences.\n- Foldables and the N series will drive premium growth, while A57/A37 and other mass-market models\nsupport shipment and revenue growth across segments. However, YoY profitability decline appears\ninevitable due to higher memory prices and other cost pressures.\n13\nSamsung Electronics (005930 KS)\n15. What is the home appliance business restructuring and profitability strategy?\n- Profitability pressure is rising from global competition, tariffs, and geopolitical risks. Samsung is\nimproving its business structure through a “selection and focus” strategy centered on core businesses.\nIt is also reviewing ways to diversify its profit structure, with details to be shared once finalized.\n16. What is the AI data center cooling market outlook and strategy after acquiring\nFläktGroup?\n- AI and HPC demand are driving structural growth in data center cooling. The market is likely o grow\nfrom about $4.7bn in 2024 to $16.6bn in 2030, implying a CAGR of roughly 24%.\n- Through the acquisition of HVAC specialist FläktGroup, Samsung has secured a strategic foothold\nin data center cooling. The business is currently Europe-focused, with expansion planned into North\nAmerica, the largest global market. Samsung also plans to establish FläktGroup’s Korean subsidiary\nand production base to diversify regions and strengthen supply capability.\n17. What is the NAND market outlook in the AI era?\n- AI adoption is increasing data storage demand, while storage demand is expanding to complement\nthe limits of HBM/DRAM-centric architectures. Demand should grow for PCIe Gen6-based high-\nperformance SSDs, TLC, and QLC.\n- Samsung is responding with high-performance TLC and high-capacity QLC products, and will\nexpand its ultra-high-capacity SSD lineup to strengthen market responsiveness.\n18. What is the impact of the TCL–Sony JV on the TV market, and Samsung’s\nresponse?\n- The TV market continues to see shifts in the competitive landscape amid stagnant demand and\nintensifying competition. A TCL–Sony JV is a foreseeable scenario, given the potential combination\nof production capacity and brand strength.\n- Samsung plans to maintain leadership by strengthening competitiveness across premium to entry-\nlevel segments. In premium, it will differentiate through new form factors such as Micro RGB; in the\nvolume zone, it will expand new Mini LED products. Samsung will also enhance consumer AI\nexperiences to strengthen product differentiation and brand competitiveness.\n19. What is the foundry investment and restructuring strategy?\n- Samsung is expanding advanced processes centered on the Taylor fab, targeting operation in 2026\nand mass production in 2027. For legacy processes, Samsung is restructuring toward high-value-\nadded specialty applications while gradually reducing inefficient lines.\n14\nCompany Report\nSamsung Electronics (005930 KS) pro
